ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Michelangelo Buonarroti — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Primary care visit for painful, stiff hands that make writing, drawing, and carving difficult

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for painful, stiff hands that make writing, drawing, and carving difficult [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: Aching, stiff hands, worst at the base of the left thumb, that make holding a chisel, a pen, or a brush hard. [S]
He will not stop carving and wants treatment that keeps him working. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Michelangelo was born at Caprese on March 6, 1475, by the modern reckoning; his father's notebook records the birth as March 6, 1474, in the Florentine style, on a Monday morning before daybreak. [D]
In 1548 he wrote to his nephew that he had lately been in great difficulty from dysuria but was better. [D]

In a letter to his nephew dated March 15, 1549, he wrote that he had been very ill with dysuria, groaning in pain night and day without sleep, that his doctors thought he was suffering from calculus, and that he had been advised to try the baths at Viterbo. [D]
On March 23, 1549, he wrote that after drinking a water sent to him he passed a large quantity of thick white matter with portions of the shell of the stone, and was much better. [D]
On April 5, 1549, he wrote that it was now quite certain that he had urinary calculus, not very advanced, and that it was gradually diminishing with the water he was drinking. [D]

In a letter the editor dates to June 8, 1549, he wrote that for about two months he had drunk, morning and evening, a water from a spring about forty miles from Rome that breaks up the stone, that it had broken his and let him pass water with tolerable ease, and that he would have to use nothing else for drinking or cooking and alter his mode of life. [D]

On June 16, 1557, he wrote to his nephew that he suffered from all the ailments of old age: the stone, so that he could not pass water, and pains in his side and back, so that he often could not go up or down stairs. [D]

A postscript to a letter of 1559 (dated June 15; the editor notes the nephew altered it to July 15) reads: writing is very troublesome to my hand, my eyes and my memory; such is the effect of age. [D]

Lazzeri and colleagues (2016), studying portraits, proposed that degenerative, non-inflammatory osteoarthritis affected the base of his left thumb, the thumb's metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints, and the index finger's metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints; earlier portraits show no deformity, and they place the onset around 1547 to 1553, with worsening in his last fifteen years. [R]

The same authors report that letters to his nephew speak of gout, a period term for many arthritic conditions, and of a cruel pain in one foot; they judged gouty arthritis of the hands unlikely because the portraits show no inflammation or tophi. [R]
His father, Lodovico, was born on June 11, 1444, and died in 1533 or 1534; Michelangelo's poem on his death says he was ninety. [D]
He had two acute illnesses, the first in the summer of 1544 and the second toward the close of 1545, when news reached Florence that he was dying; he recovered from both. [D]

text.paragraph: 3 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

text.paragraph: Positive for the concerns in the history of present illness. Alert, intense, and exacting; impatient with anything that keeps him from work. Mood steady; cognition intact. No other systems reported as affected in this synthetic episode. [S]

Hand exercise and joint protection: daily thumb-stabilizing and range-of-motion exercises, padded and thicker tool handles, a lighter mallet, and rest breaks during carving, taught in a course of occupational hand therapy. Guideline: 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis monograph (2026) [S]

Hand-based thumb splint for the left first carpometacarpal joint during heavy work and at night. Guideline: 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis monograph (2026) [S]

Stop over-the-counter ibuprofen; use topical diclofenac gel first and acetaminophen as needed up to 3 g a day; avoid regular oral NSAIDs at his age because of kidney, blood pressure, bleeding, and gout risks; recheck creatinine in four weeks. Guideline: 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); American Geriatrics Society 2023 Updated AGS Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis monograph (2026) [S]

Rheumatology consultation to confirm hand osteoarthritis, exclude inflammatory and crystal arthritis, and advise on a thumb-base glucocorticoid injection and further options. Guideline: 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis monograph (2026) [S]

CMID osteoarthritis monitoring: pain rating, a validated function measure, grip strength, and joint examination at each visit; ALT when acetaminophen is used regularly; creatinine, blood count, and blood pressure if oral NSAIDs are ever used; no routine repeat radiographs; periodic mood and sleep screening. Guideline: 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis monograph (2026) [S]

Continue allopurinol 200 mg daily with serum urate every six months at target; drink at least 2 L of water a day to prevent stones. Guideline: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout (2020); Medical Management of Kidney Stones: AUA Guideline (2014, amended 2019) [S]

Falls prevention: platform ladder with a rail, never climbing alone, good studio lighting, and a yearly fall-risk check. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis monograph (2026) [S]
